name: the finished site tilts into view with a glowing edge
looks: A full interface panel swings into a fixed, shallow 3D tilt, lit by a single accent-coloured glow around its edge. The page scrolls to reveal its sections -- a headline statement, a row of short principle cards -- while two more faint copies of the same panel sit stacked slightly behind it, as if several passes of the same page exist at once.
build: A DOM panel inside a perspective parent, rotateX/rotateY fixed with a slow degree or two of drift; a shared glow class marks its border; the panel's inner content scrolls/cross-fades through its sections; two further instances of the same panel sit offset behind at reduced opacity.
sound: A soft slide as the panel settles into its tilt, quiet under the scroll.
prompt: Tilt a finished interface panel into a fixed, shallow 3D angle with one accent-coloured glow tracing its live edge, then scroll through its sections while a couple of fainter duplicate panels sit stacked behind it -- read as 'here is the finished, polished result, and there were other passes before it.'
